footnotes: Banks have no cost of sales; the flow chart shows revenue (net interest income + noninterest income) going to noninterest expense and the provision for credit losses, leaving pre-tax income. Other items, net are the gains and charges the income statement shows outside these lines (−$55.0M in 2025). From pre-tax income to net income to common: after income tax and $228M of preferred dividends & other. Efficiency ratio = noninterest expense ÷ revenue (lower is better).
Figures are from the company's Form 10-K for fiscal years ended Dec 31, 2025 and a year earlier, as filed with the SEC. Never estimated: items the filing does not report are left out.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Revenue (net interest income plus noninterest income) rose 6.6% to $13.9B in 2025. Net interest income rose 1.3% to $3.0B and noninterest income rose 8.1% to $11.0B; noninterest expense rose 6.5%, and the provision for credit losses was $0, versus $0.
Net income to common rose 9.4% to $2.7B, or $9.40 per diluted share, and the efficiency ratio was 72.8% versus 72.9%. State Street returned $2.3B through dividends and buybacks.
highlights: Net income to common rose 9.4% to $2.7B.
watch: Net interest income depends on interest rates.
sources: State Street Corporation Form 10-K for FY2025 (SEC EDGAR)
